evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=52.0 h = 7.41 mg/L; minimum over last 10 h ~7.39 mg/L, well above 2.0 mg/L constraint
Receiving P(48 h) assay = 3.025 g/L vs source-1 3.057, source-2 3.017, source-3 2.979 g/L at same time point
Receiving DO2 trajectory (dip at ~24 h, recovery at 28 h, second dip from ~46 h) matches all three source batches, which reached P ~8 g/L at 72 h with no oxygen violations
Allowed action bounds: keep = [1.0, 1.0]; no bounded intervention improves on baseline given unconstrained DO2 and on-track product formation
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation is performing normally. DO2 (~7.4 mg/L at t=52 h, never below ~7.4 mg/L in the recent window) is far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and the delayed product assay P(48 h)=3.025 g/L matches the source batches (3.0-3.06 g/L) at the same point, all of which went on to peak near 8 g/L without intervention. No oxygen-constraint violation exists or is imminent. Any feed reduction would sacrifice product mass, and increased aeration is unnecessary since oxygen is not limiting. Normal case: no intervention needed.
args.uncertainty: Receiving parameters may differ from the source processes, so future DO2/product trajectory is not guaranteed; the second DO2 sag could deepen after 52 h. However, the assay agreement and matching trajectory give moderate-to-high confidence that KEEP preserves the most product mass while avoiding constraint risk. If DO2 were to approach ~2 mg/L, aeration increase would become the preferred bounded intervention.
